title: World population reaches 1 billion
detail: It took all of human history to reach this milestone. The next billion would take just 127 years.

title: Napoleon crowns himself Emperor
detail: Europe's borders are redrawn by ambition. The ripple effects will reshape law, language, and nationalism for centuries.

title: Luddites smash machines
detail: Workers in England destroy textile machinery, fearing automation will take their jobs. The first clash between progress and people.

title: Year Without a Summer
detail: Mount Tambora's eruption blankets the globe in ash. Crop failures trigger famine across Europe and North America.

title: First public railway opens
detail: The Stockton and Darlington Railway carries passengers at 15 mph. The world will soon shrink beyond recognition.

title: First cholera pandemic reaches Europe
detail: The disease kills tens of thousands. It will take decades before germ theory replaces miasma as the accepted explanation.

title: Victoria becomes Queen
detail: Her reign will span 63 years and define an era of empire, industry, and contradiction — progress for some, oppression for many.

title: Mines Act bans child labour underground
detail: Children under 10 can no longer work in British mines. The first crack in the wall of unfettered industrial capitalism.

title: Communist Manifesto published
detail: Marx and Engels write: 'The history of all hitherto existing society is the history of class struggles.' It will reshape the century.

title: Nightingale goes to Crimea
detail: Florence Nightingale transforms military medicine. Her statistical charts will prove that cleanliness saves more lives than combat.

title: On the Origin of Species
detail: Darwin publishes the theory of evolution by natural selection. It will take a century for the full implications to sink in.

title: Slavery abolished in the United States
detail: The 13th Amendment ends 246 years of legal chattel slavery. But true freedom remains decades away.

title: Suez Canal opens
detail: Ships no longer need to sail around Africa. Global trade routes are rewritten in a single stroke.

title: Bell patents the telephone
detail: Alexander Graham Bell's invention will, within a century, connect every person on Earth.

title: Edison demonstrates the light bulb
detail: Electric light will reshape cities, factories, and the very rhythm of human life.

title: Edison opens Pearl Street Station
detail: The first commercial power station lights lower Manhattan. The age of electricity begins.

title: Koch identifies tuberculosis bacillus
detail: The leading killer of the 19th century is finally understood. A vaccine will take another 60 years.

title: X-rays discovered
detail: Wilhelm Roentgen sees through flesh for the first time. Medicine will never be the same.

title: Boer War begins
detail: Britain fights Dutch settlers in South Africa. The war exposes the brutality of empire — and the power of concentration camps.

title: First powered flight
detail: The Wright brothers fly for 12 seconds at Kitty Hawk. Within 66 years, humans will walk on the Moon.

title: Einstein publishes special relativity
detail: Space and time are no longer absolute. The physics of the universe is rewritten by a 26-year-old patent clerk.

title: Ford Model T makes cars affordable
detail: Mass production cuts the price from $850 to $260. Mobility becomes a right, not a privilege.

title: Titanic sinks
detail: 1,500 die on a ship called unsinkable. hubris meets the ocean, and the Gilded Age drowns with it.

title: World War I begins
detail: The war to end all wars kills over 35 million. Trenches, gas, and machine guns turn Europe into a graveyard.

title: Spanish Flu kills 50 million
detail: The deadliest pandemic in modern history kills more people than World War I had in four years of trenches.

title: Women gain the right to vote in the US
detail: The 19th Amendment passes after 72 years of activism. Suffragists finally see the ballot.

title: Penicillin discovered
detail: Alexander Fleming notices a mold killing bacteria. Antibiotics will save an estimated 200 million lives.

title: Wall Street crashes
detail: The Great Depression begins. Unemployment reaches 25%. The promise of prosperity collapses overnight.

title: Hitler becomes Chancellor of Germany
detail: Democracy elects its own destroyer. The consequences will engulf the entire world.

title: Japan invades China
detail: The Rape of Nanking claims 200,000 lives. The Pacific theater of World War II has quietly begun.

title: World War II begins
detail: The deadliest conflict in human history. 70-85 million dead. The world will never again see war on this scale.

title: Manhattan Project begins
detail: The US government hires 125,000 people to build an atomic bomb. Science becomes a weapon of mass destruction.

title: United Nations founded
detail: From the ruins of war, 51 nations pledge to 'save succeeding generations from the scourge of war.' The modern international order begins.

title: India gains independence
detail: Gandhi's non-violent resistance topples an empire. 400 million people are freed. Partition kills 2 million.

title: Universal Declaration of Human Rights
detail: Eleanor Roosevelt calls it 'a Magna Carta for all mankind.' For the first time, the world agrees on what every person deserves.

title: Korean War begins
detail: The Cold War turns hot. 3 million die on a peninsula most Americans cannot find on a map.

title: DNA structure discovered
detail: Watson and Crick reveal the double helix. The code of life is cracked.

title: Sputnik launches the Space Age
detail: A Soviet satellite beeps from orbit. The US panics. Space becomes the ultimate frontier of competition.

title: Green Revolution begins
detail: Norman Borlaug's high-yield wheat varieties will save an estimated billion lives from famine.

title: Cuban Missile Crisis
detail: The world comes within 13 minutes of nuclear war. Kennedy and Khrushchev blink simultaneously.

title: Civil Rights Act signed
detail: Martin Luther King Jr. pushes America toward its own ideals. The law now says what morality always should have.

title: Cultural Revolution begins in China
detail: Mao's purge destroys cultural heritage and sends millions to labor camps. A decade of chaos follows.

title: Moon landing
detail: Neil Armstrong takes one small step. 600 million people watch live. The impossible becomes routine.

title: Club of Rome warns of limits
detail: 'Limits to Growth' predicts ecological collapse if trends continue. The world largely ignores the warning.

title: Fall of Saigon
detail: The Vietnam War ends after 20 years, 58,000 American lives, and 2 million Vietnamese dead. The superpower learns humility.

title: Smallpox eradicated
detail: The only human disease ever completely wiped out. A triumph of global cooperation.

title: Iranian Revolution
detail: The Shah falls. Theocracy rises. US-Iran relations freeze for decades.

title: HIV/AIDS identified
detail: The epidemic will kill 40 million people. It will take decades and unprecedented drug access programs to bring it under control.

title: Chernobyl disaster
detail: The worst nuclear accident in history. 350,000 people are evacuated. The Soviet Union's decline accelerates.

title: Fall of the Berlin Wall
detail: The Cold War ends not with a bang but with hammers and chisels. 28 years of division dissolve in a single night.

title: World Wide Web goes public
detail: Tim Berners-Lee makes the internet free for everyone. Information, for the first time, has no gatekeeper.

title: Apartheid ends in South Africa
detail: Nelson Mandela walks free after 27 years. South Africa holds its first multiracial election. The world watches in awe.

title: Millennium Development Goals
detail: 189 nations commit to 8 goals: halve poverty, achieve universal education, stop HIV/AIDS. It is the largest anti-poverty effort in history.

title: September 11 attacks
detail: 2,977 die. The US launches wars in Afghanistan and Iraq that will last two decades and cost trillions.

title: Human Genome Project completed
detail: Every gene in the human body is mapped. The blueprint of our species is written down.

title: Indian Ocean tsunami
detail: 230,000 die in the deadliest tsunami in recorded history. Early warning systems are built in its aftermath.

title: Global financial crisis
detail: Banks collapse. 8 million jobs vanish. The worst economic disaster since the Great Depression.

title: Extreme poverty halves
detail: The MDG target for poverty is met 5 years early. 1 billion people lifted out of extreme poverty since 1990.

title: Arab Spring
detail: Protests sweep the Middle East. Dictators fall. But democracy takes root in only some soil.

title: Sustainable Development Goals adopted
detail: 17 goals, 169 targets, one deadline: 2030. The most ambitious plan humanity has ever agreed to.

title: Paris Agreement enters force
detail: 196 nations agree to limit warming to 1.5C. Whether they follow through is another question.

title: COVID-19 pandemic
detail: Global life expectancy drops for the first time in decades. But vaccines are developed in record time — 327 days from sequence to injection.

title: Global extreme poverty returns
detail: COVID, Ukraine, and inflation push 75 million more people into extreme poverty. The first reversal in decades.

title: Child mortality reaches historic low
detail: 35 per 1,000, down from 460 in 1800. The greatest improvement in human welfare ever recorded.
